passage:
The placement office smelled of printer ink. Hrithik stood at the notice board staring at his name under a Mumbai firm, and his first feeling was not joy but a cold knot.
Mehak was in her final year in Delhi. For two years they had said 'we'll figure it out after graduation' and changed the subject. Each time, he had been scared she'd say she would never leave Delhi. He found out later that she had been scared he'd say the same about his hometown.
He called her from the corridor. 'Got placed. Mumbai.'
A pause. 'Congratulations.' Another pause. 'So that's decided, then.'
'Nothing's decided.'
'You applied to Mumbai, Hrithik. You never asked me.'
'You never said anything either.'
The corridor filled with students cheering each other. Hrithik held the phone and listened to two years of unspoken questions arrive at once.

qa.q: Which city was Hrithik's placement in?
What was Hrithik feeling as he stared at his name, and why?
qa.a: He felt a cold knot of dread instead of joy, because the question of where they would live had never been faced.

qa.q: What could the couple have done a year earlier?
qa.a: Sit down and talk honestly about where each hoped to live after graduation, with a few possible options, before applying anywhere.

qa.q: How does the placement news feel to Mehak?
qa.a: She feels hurt and resentful, since a big decision seems made without her, even though she also avoided the topic.

grounding: Shows a couple who never discussed where they would live after graduation, so vague hope turns into resentment when a placement arrives.

passage:
Dear Afreen,
You asked why Sameer and I were so tense at your birthday. I'll try to explain, because I've only just understood it myself.
We've been long-distance for three years, me in Kolkata, him in Bengaluru. Every time someone asked 'so what's the plan after college?', we'd both laugh and say 'we'll see'. I told myself that was trust. Really, I was scared that if I asked, he'd say he'd never move east, and I'd have to choose.
At your party someone joked about who would move for whom. Sameer went quiet, and I snapped at him for no reason. On the train back I saw that I've been angry with him for months over a conversation we've never had.
I'm going to ask him properly this weekend. I'm terrified, but the not-knowing is worse.
Love,
Aadhya

qa.q: How long have Aadhya and Sameer been long-distance?
What was Aadhya really scared of all this time?
qa.a: Aadhya was afraid that asking would lead Sameer to say he'd never move east, forcing a choice, so avoiding it felt safer.

qa.q: What would you advise Aadhya for the talk this weekend?
qa.a: Pick a calm time, share the fear honestly, and explore a few possible options together instead of demanding one answer.

qa.q: How might Sameer have felt when Aadhya snapped at him at the party?
qa.a: He was probably confused and hurt, not knowing the snap came from months of unspoken worry.

grounding: Shows a couple who kept saying 'we'll see' about life after college until the unasked question turned into anger.
